title: Partner cloud listing preflight cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
A compact prelaunch checklist and copy guidance for partner marketplace listings (AWS/GCP/Azure and cloud vendor marketplaces). Designed for GTM, partner reps, and engineering owners preparing a listing draft for review. This is intentionally pragmatic — quick acceptance criteria, examples, and the top reasons a submission gets rejected plus remediation notes.

Audience:
- Partner marketing/product managers
- Redwood partner ops and listing owners
- Solutions engineers (asset collection)
- Legal/compliance reviewers (quick reference)

Quick acceptance heuristic (pass/fail):
- Metadata complete (title, short+long descriptions, 3 feature bullets): PASS
- Assets present (logo, 3 screenshots, one hero image): PASS
- Pricing/SKU mapping declared and matches vendor form: PASS
- Security & data residency notes included if required for private deployments: PASS
- Responsible owner assigned with contact info: PASS
If any are FAIL, list remediation and resubmit.

Preflight checklist (actionable items):
1) Listing metadata
   - Official product title (max 60 chars) and an alternate display name if needed for vendor UI.
   - Short description (1 sentence, 140–200 chars) focused on value: who + key outcome + one differentiator.
   - Long description (3–6 short paragraphs): how it works, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and primary integrations.
   - 3 feature bullets (one-line each): performance, reliability, cost controls (e.g., batching/caching), and SLA/commitments.
   - Version & pinned model info (if applicable): specify model family and whether quantized variant is listed.

2) Asset checklist (filename conventions recommended)
   - Logo (square, 512px) — file: redwood-logo-square.png
   - Hero banner (1600x600 recommended) — file: redwood-hero-marketplace.jpg
   - 3 screenshots with captions (1280x720): product-console-1.png, rollout-dashboard.png, cost-breakdown.png
   - Alt text for each image (1-line) included in submission form.
   - One short demo GIF (optional) <10s for UI flows.

3) Pricing and SKUs
   - Mapping document attached: vendor SKU -> Redwood billing SKU -> unit metric (tokens/minute, embeddings/1000).
   - Clear notes for reserved capacity (Dedicated) vs. usage-based hosted pricing and any minimum commitments.
   - Trial credits or free-tier offer copy if applicable.

4) Compliance & Security (must include short statements)
   - Data handling summary (what is logged, retention period, customer-controlled keys if Private).
   - Regional availability flags (US, EU, APAC) and any latent limitations.
   - Certifications (SOC2, ISO27001) — link to compliance page or evidence.

5) Support & SLA
   - Support channels (email, Slack, ticketing) and hours (business hours/24x7).
   - SLA summary: uptime target and latency guidance per SKU.

6) Legal & Terms
   - Link to terms of service and privacy policy specific to listing.
   - Any partner co-marketing language and attribution requirements.

Copy guidelines (tone + structure):
- Tone: concise, technical-credible, product-first. Prefer short, declarative sentences. Avoid marketing hyperbole like "best" or "revolutionary" without quantifiable claims.
- SEO keywords (vendor-specific): marketplace, inference, low-latency LLM inference, dedicated GPU serving, private deployment, predictable throughput. Insert naturally in the long description.
- First paragraph of long description should summarize deployment options and primary business outcomes (latency, cost predictability, reliability).
- Always include an example use-case paragraph (2–3 sentences) showing an industry or developer persona and the outcome.

Field-by-field sample copy (templates to copy/paste):
- Short description (example): "High-throughput, low-latency LLM inference for production applications — served hosted, reserved, or private with built-in cost and reliability controls."
- Long description lead (example): "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for serving large language models across hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployments. Ship features that require predictable latency and cost: streaming responses, function/tool calling, and model rollouts with observability."
- Feature bullets (examples):
   • Predictable latency: optimized runtime and smart routing to meet tail-SLOs.
   • Cost controls: intelligent batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations.
   • Enterprise-ready: dedicated capacity, VPC/private deployments, and audit logs.
- Use case snippet (example): "Customer support platforms reduce average handle time by 30% with streaming answers and model fallbacks during peak traffic."

QA heuristics (things reviewers should look for):
- Does the short description explicitly state the product category (inference / LLM)?
- Are all screenshots clearly labeled and reflect the actual UI customers will see?
- Is there a clear differentiation between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in copy and pricing?
- Are any absolute guarantees made that require legal review (e.g., "100% accuracy")? Flag and revise.
- Are links valid and publicly accessible or gated appropriately (docs vs internal drafts)?

Top rejection reasons and remediation notes: 
- Missing assets: return for asset upload; list exact filenames required.
- Ambiguous pricing: request detailed SKU mapping and a sample invoice calculation.
- Security claims without evidence: request SOC2/ISO artifacts or remove claims.
- Copy too marketing-y: replace with technical/use-case focused language.
- Screenshots show internal-only data or PII: redact and resubmit.

Acceptance scoring rubric (quick 0–10):
- Metadata completeness: 0–3 pts
- Asset quality & alt text: 0–2 pts
- Pricing clarity: 0–2 pts
- Compliance & links: 0–2 pts
- Final pass threshold: >=8

Owners & timeline (recommended):
- Partner PM: gather assets + initial draft — 3 business days.
- Redwood partner ops: review metadata + pricing mapping — 2 business days.
- Legal/security: compliance signoff — 3–5 business days (parallel).
- Final listing submission by partner ops — 1 business day.

Mini checklist to attach with submissions (copyable):
[ ] Title & short/long descriptions written
[ ] 3 feature bullets
[ ] Logo + hero + 3 screenshots uploaded with alt text
[ ] Pricing SKU mapping attached
[ ] Data handling statement included
[ ] Support/SLA blurb included
[ ] Owner name & contact provided

Notes to engineers/SREs:
- If listing mentions specific latency SLOs, include a small note on measured benchmarks (p50/p95 with test harness link).
- For Dedicated/private options, provide region availability matrix and a simple deployment guide link.

Examples of small fixes (editor tips):
- Change passive to active voice: "is provided by" -> "provides".
- Replace vague phrase "enterprise customers" with a concrete persona: "security-conscious fintech teams".
- Avoid internal product abbreviations without expansion on first use (e.g., "RBW" -> "Redwood Inference (RBW)").

Appendix: quick links and references
- Redwood marketplace standards (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GT/Marketplace+Listing+Standards
- Compliance evidence tracker: JIRA-4821
- Asset repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets

Notes to reviewer: this doc is a living cheatsheet — copy and paste the sample snippets into vendor forms and update the acceptance rubric if new vendor demands appear.
